summary: Iteration 18 — end-to-end verification of the reworked review-reward flow (coupon issued only on APPROVAL, not on submit; decline is hard-delete + order locked; auto coupons kept for 30d after redemption; single-use, issued_to-locked). New pytest file /app/backend/tests/test_review_rewards_v10.py covers 9 backend scenarios (submit-no-coupon, approve-issues-one-coupon, 1-star still gets coupon, re-approve is a no-op, decline path + review_declined flag, single-use validate after redemption keeps the row, wrong-email rejection, admin coupon delete -> reviews/status coupon.state='unavailable', 30-day sweep keeps recent/redeemed and long-lived unredeemed rows, only deletes 30d+ redeemed OR expired). All 9 pass. Playwright then drove the full customer→admin→customer loop against the preview URL with the seeded reviewqa_8787@gmail.com account and the officialwifi@icloud.com admin: submit a review on order A shows the review-coupon-pending panel with NO coupon code and MyOrders flips to review-submitted-<id>; approve fires POST /admin/reviews/{id}/approve returning coupon THANKSE95380, the toast surfaces the code, order B gets declined (row removed, order locked, no button rendered on MyOrders), Coupons/auto tab renders coupon-status-THANKSE95380 = 'unredeemed', MyOrders review-coupon-<order> shows 'COUPON CREDITED · THANKSE95380 · 5% OFF', and after the admin deletes the auto coupon the same slot switches to review-coupon-unavailable-<order>. Backend + frontend both green — no bugs found in the reworked feature.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1724 lines — well past the 700-line guideline. The review/coupon block (sweep_auto_coupons, issue_review_coupon, coupon_state, review_status, approve/delete review, notify_review_approved) is a clean, ~200-line unit and would move out to /app/backend/reviews.py or /app/backend/coupons.py without touching call sites — good candidate for the next split.

record_redemption swallows ALL exceptions with a plain logger.error — if the coupons collection is briefly unavailable during a paid webhook the customer keeps the coupon usable for a second order. Consider narrowing except Exception to pymongo errors and re-raising anything unexpected so the webhook retries.

coupon_state assumes stored expires_at is naive UTC and adds tzinfo before comparing — works today because Mongo strips tz on write, but any future writer using timezone-aware datetimes would trigger 'can't compare offset-naive and offset-aware' via replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc). load_coupon does exactly the same thing; both should switch to `expires_at if expires_at.tzinfo else expires_at.replace(tzinfo=timezone.utc)` for safety.

approve_review is not concurrency-safe: two admins clicking Approve at the same time can both pass the `already_approved` check and each issue a coupon (the update_one that sets status/approved_at is not conditional on the prior status). Suggest `find_one_and_update({..., 'status': 'pending'}, ...)` and only issue a coupon when the doc pre-update was pending.

issue_review_coupon relies on a DuplicateKeyError retry — the coupons collection must have a unique index on `code` for the collision guard to work. Please confirm the index exists in production (`db.coupons.getIndexes()`), otherwise a collision would silently create a duplicate row and load_coupon would resolve arbitrarily.
